LETTER FROM THE PRESIDENT AND CEO
Dear Shareholders:
2016 PERFORMANCE
As we look back on 2016, I am pleased with the year-over-year improvement in our operating results as we continue to focus
on increasing shareholder value. We are reporting double digit increases in net income and earnings per share, good growth
in loans and deposits, solid credit quality metrics, and strong capital ratios. For the year ended December 31, 2016, the
Company reported net income of $22.8 million, or $1.05 per diluted share, compared to net income of $20.0 million, or
$0.86 per diluted share, in 2015.
Earnings: Striving for Sustained Long-Term Growth
Our earnings are a critical component to the valuation of our Company. This past year we achieved a 13.7% increase in net
income and a 22.1% increase in diluted earnings per share. For the full year, our return on assets improved to 0.92% from
0.86% while our return on average common shareholders’ equity improved to 9.21% from 7.89% one year ago. At
December 31, 2016, our tangible book value per share increased by 3.9% to $11.62, up from $11.18 one year ago.
Balance sheet: Diversified, Liquid, and Asset Sensitive
Our balance sheet continues to show real strength, with a good mix of earning assets, a growing core deposit base, a
72.3% loans-to-deposits ratio and a bias towards rising interest rates (asset sensitive). For the full year, loans grew by
$127.8 million, or 8.6% (excluding payment plan receivables). All three loan categories, commercial, mortgage and
installment, increased for the second consecutive year. For all of 2016, the commercial team generated $288.8 million
of new commitments growing our commercial loan portfolio by $55.6 million, or 7.4%. Overall, we continue to have a
nice mix of new business by region and by segment, and improved operating leverage for the commercial banking group.
Our mortgage team originated $428.2 million of loans and we sold $314.0 million during 2016. This compares favorably to
2015, when we originated $336.6 million and had sales of $281.5 million. This represents a 27.2% increase in originations
and an 11.5% increase in sales. For all of 2016, portfolio mortgages increased by $40.6 million, or 8.1%. I am particularly
pleased that nearly two-thirds of our 2016 mortgage closings represented purchase money

Total deposits were $2.23 billion at December 31, 2016, an increase of $139.8 million, or 6.7% since December 31, 2015.
The increase in deposits occurred across our geographic markets in retail, commercial and public funds categories. The
Company’s deposit base is substantially all core funding with $1.74 billion or 78.2% in transaction accounts. This reflects
the significant value of our franchise, with a cost of deposits to total deposits of 0.25% for the fourth quarter of 2016.
Credit Quality: Strong
Maintaining prudent credit standards will always be a top priority for our Company. Our thirty- to eighty -nine day delinquency
rates at December 31, 2016, were zero for commercial loans and 0.66% for mortgage and consumer loans. At year- end
2016, the ratio of non-performing assets to total assets improved to 0.72% from 0.74% one year ago, while our allowance for
loan losses was $20.2 million or 1.26% of loans. I am very pleased to see our loan net charge-offs continue to be low. Loan
net charge-offs to average portfolio loans for all of 2016 were 0.06% compared to 0.05% in 2015.

Other Matters: Continued Focus on Community Banking
In December of 2016, we signed an agreement to sell the majority of the assets and the payment processing business of
Mepco Finance Corporation, our Chicago-based subsidiary. Mepco had become a non-strategic asset during the last few
years, and we believe this divestiture will allow us to completely focus on our community banking business. We expect to
close on this transaction during the first half of 2017.
In the later part of last year, we made a significant investment in our mortgage banking business. This effort included the
adding of approximately fifty new associates and the opening of five new loan production offices. These offices are located
in Ann Arbor, Brighton, Traverse City and Troy, Michigan and in Columbus, Ohio. In 2017, we have opened additional loan
production offices in Dearborn, Michigan and Fairlawn, Ohio. We believe each of these markets provide solid growth
opportunities for our Company.
We were also very pleased to have Ms. Christina Keller join our Board of Directors in December of 2016. Ms. Keller’s
experience working in a leadership role at a global manufacturing company headquartered in West Michigan, her
international experience, and educational background, make her an important addition to our Board.
COMMUNITY BANKING & OUR MARKETS
Macro Environment: Directional Change, from Headwinds to Tailwinds; and Uncertainty
There has been a real shift in the macro economic outlook from years past. Today, there exists significant optimism for
the banking industry, particularly following the November 2016 elections. The optimism stems from a belief in a more
accommodating business environment, rising interest rates, a steepening yield curve, tax reform and regulatory relief.
Whether one or more of these factors materializes is yet unknown; however, in the interim, bank stock valuations have
priced in some benefit from these potential changes.

Local Markets: Positive Trends Continue
Independent Bank is the fourth largest bank headquartered in the State of Michigan. We operate 63 branches in 21 counties
across Michigan’s Lower Peninsula. In addition, we operate 14 loan production offices, generally in markets that we believe to
offer strong growth potential.
2016 was the sixth consecutive year that the State reported an increase in payroll jobs and the seventh consecutive year that
Michigan’s unemployment rate moved lower. At year end, the Michigan jobless rate was 5.0%, or one-tenth of a percentage
point below the State’s December 2015 unemployment rate of 5.1%. Michigan payroll jobs totaled 4.41 million at December
31, 2016, 90,000 jobs higher than one year ago. We also continue to see positive year-over-year trends in home sales, home
prices, and housing starts in most of our markets. Commercial real estate occupancy rates in office, industrial and retail are
also either stable or trending positive.

Operating Plan
We are now operating near our previously established profitability targets, 1.0% return on assets and 10.0% or better return on
equity. However, sustaining this level and in fact improving on it each year is our number one goal. Our operating plan going
forward continues to be straight forward and very consistent with what I have shared in the past.
First, we seek to further improve net interest income through loan growth and altering our interest-earning asset mix from lower
yielding investment securities to higher yielding loans. We believe this lever or opportunity still exists as we work towards an
85% to 95% loan-to-deposit ratio. Our recent move to expand our mortgage banking area with loan production offices in
higher growth, more densely populated markets directly feeds this objective. In fact, as you may recall, I shared in my 2015
shareholder letter our decision to invest in the industry’s premier mortgage loan origination platform, as we remain committed
to mortgage lending, while others in the banking industry were deciding to exit the business. We believe that despite a higher
interest rate environment in the forecast, our on-going emphasis on purchase money transactions will serve us well to generate
gains and servicing income on saleable loans, in addition to interest income on non-saleable portfolio originations. This
expansion effort, combined with continued growth in our existing commercial banking and consumer banking business

diversification in our loan portfolios.

Finally, capital management will continue to be a priority for us. I regularly share our targeted tangible common equity to tangible
assets ratio of 8.5% to 9.5%. This range takes into consideration the growth opportunities in front of us, as well as the inherent
risks of our balance sheet and longer-term capital needs. Our priorities will be organic growth, followed by a consistent dividend
with a payout range of 30% to 50% of earnings; followed by share repurchases in consideration of an acceptable earn back
period. Acquired growth on an opportunistic basis will also be considered.
Again, this operating plan of accelerating revenue growth, controlling expenses, always seeking to grow our core deposit base,
investing in our people, while managing risk and being good stewards of our capital, is very consistent with the plan shared
in years past. The key to our ongoing efforts is in sound execution of this plan, which can only be accomplished with great
teamwork. I am very proud of the Independent Bank team and have a great deal of confidence in them to successfully
execute our plan.
CLOSING
I encourage you to attend the 2017 Annual Meeting of Shareholders of Independent Bank Corporation at 3:00 p.m. Eastern
Time, on Tuesday, April 25, 2017. For the third consecutive year, and as a convenience to all of our shareholders, we will
be conducting our Annual Meeting of Shareholders, virtually, by means of remote communication via the internet.
In closing, I would like to acknowledge the commitment and ongoing effort of your Board of Directors, our Bank officers, and
all of our Bank associates. Their dedication and service is exemplary, and each is truly making a positive difference in the
lives of our customers, our shareholders, and the communities we serve.
